html:
SMTO-EXE-0211 — SMTO couldn't find the saved password for this PDF

GUID: b7fb28c0-6a12-5c6c-bd8a-7c810371b180
Slug: pdf-password-reference-invalid
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • The PDF needs a password, but SMTO couldn't match it to exactly one saved PDF password mentioned in your message. Nothing was opened or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, choose PDF password in the template list, select New, enter the password, and select Save. SMTO only uses PDF passwords saved with this template, never ones typed into the chat.
  2. In a new message, mention the saved password with @ followed by its exact name, and ask for the PDF action. SMTO can only use saved passwords that your message mentions by name.
  3. If you're combining several protected PDFs, save and mention a separate password entry for each file. Each protected file is unlocked with its own saved password.
  4. If you already had an entry, check it was made from the PDF password template and still has a password filled in. An entry of a different type or with an empty password can't be used for PDFs.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens the protected PDF and completes the action you asked for.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the name of the saved password you mentioned, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the password itself into the chat or the error report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The PDF password_ref did not match exactly one pdf_password binding accepted for this task, the accepted value could not be recovered or validated, or the Gateway worker did not receive the private value.

What this means

  • A password_ref did not resolve to exactly one accepted binding of type pdf_password, its accepted revision could not be recovered/validated, or the worker lacked its private value. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • A password_ref did not resolve to exactly one accepted binding of type pdf_password, its accepted revision could not be recovered/validated, or the worker lacked its private value.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the public reference key, accepted typed binding and revision availability; never substitute an unaccepted newer value.

How to fix it

  • Create or select a Parameter Store record using the pdf_password template, mention its exact key with @ in a new prompt so it becomes an accepted binding, and pass that key as password_ref. Each encrypted source in a merge or insert needs its own accepted reference; the value must be a valid pdf_password profile (password field present).
  • Accept the intended existing typed pdf_password reference and pass only its exact key; multi-source work must resolve each needed reference separately.

Retry and execution caution

  • Accept exactly one existing typed pdf_password reference. Use its exact key as password_ref.

How to verify the fix

  • Each source's required exact reference resolves privately under its accepted revision.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
